conventions.convention: BV functions are real L1 almost-everywhere classes; D_i u acts by minus the integral of u times the test derivative. Vector variation uses the Euclidean norm and countable Borel partitions. Finite perimeter requires an integrable indicator.
Neumann TV counts only interior variation; Dirichlet TV is full-space variation of the zero extension, or infinity if that extension is not BV.
Graph surface measure is repository Hausdorff measure divided by c_m = H^m((0,1]^m); the epigraph outward normal is (Dh,−1)/sqrt(1+|Dh|²).
Bounded Lipschitz domains have finite one-sided Lipschitz graph covers; connectedness is an additional hypothesis where stated. Dimension-one boundary measure is counting measure.
Coarea uses positive superlevels {u>t} for t>0 and negative sublevels {u<t} for t<0, keeping the level indicators integrable on unbounded domains.

The finite-test-supremum characterization for arbitrary L1 functions assumes Countable Choice; the test formula and lower semicontinuity when the functions and limit are already BV are stated without Choice.
Sequence compactness is proved under Countable Choice using deterministic cell-coefficient selection, without assuming Dependent Choice.

load_bearing.statement: For u∈BV(Ω), TV(u;Ω) is the supremum of ∫u div φ over smooth compactly supported vector fields with |φ|≤1, and is lower semicontinuous under L1 convergence with BV limit. Assuming Countable Choice, finiteness of this supremum for real u∈L1(Ω) is equivalent to u∈BV(Ω); an L1 limit with bounded liminf variation is BV and satisfies the same inequality.

Assuming Countable Choice, a locally Lipschitz scalar function on an open subset of R^m is differentiable almost everywhere, with measurable weak derivatives; normalized graph area has density sqrt(1+|Dh|²), and epigraph divergence flux has vector density (Dh,−1).

Assuming Countable Choice, a bounded Lipschitz domain admits a unique bounded linear BV trace satisfying the stated Green identity, and TV of zero extension equals interior TV plus the boundary L1 trace norm, bounded by a domain constant times the BV norm. The stated finite-boundary dimension-one companion also holds.
Assume Countable Choice. For every open Ω⊆R^n and u∈BV(Ω), there are smooth u_k converging to u in L1 with ∫|∇u_k|→TV(u;Ω). In full space the approximants may be compactly supported.

Assuming Countable Choice, for u∈BV(Ω) on any open Ω, positive superlevels and negative sublevels have finite relative perimeter for almost every applicable level, and their two perimeter integrals sum to TV(u;Ω).

Assuming Countable Choice, zero extension on a bounded Lipschitz domain has bounded full-space BV norm and support in the domain closure; every full-space BV function satisfies ||v(·+h)−v||1≤|h|TV(v).

Assuming Countable Choice, every sequence on a bounded Lipschitz domain with uniformly bounded L1 norm plus total variation has an L1-convergent subsequence with BV limit; total variation is L1 lower semicontinuous.

concerns.concern: F1 says 'Products of nonnegative measurable functions can be integrated iteratively by Tonelli’s theorem', and Step 1.2 applies it to the merely Lebesgue-measurable g_i from the Statement. The cited thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces requires product measurability; it does not itself identify higher-dimensional Lebesgue measure with the completed product or justify these sections. The batch elsewhere explicitly uses the completed-product suppliers, which assume Countable Choice. Supply the Borel-representative/completion argument and account for its axiom requirements here. The ordinary Loomis–Whitney calculation is sound once this transfer is justified.

F3 states 'Dominated convergence holds on Lebesgue measure spaces without a choice assumption', and Step 2.1 uses Lebesgue convolution integrals to establish this unqualified density result. The cited dominated-convergence theorem assumes an existing measure space; it does not establish the Euclidean Lebesgue-measure interface without Choice. The repository's Lebesgue Radon and convolution suppliers explicitly assume Countable Choice. Since every integrand here is continuous with compact support, a direct compact-support Riemann-integral/uniform-difference-quotient argument should close this small gap while retaining the choice-free statement.

seams_checked.note: Checked the downstream uses against their suppliers. The page distinguishes full-space L2 test variation from globally L1 BV, supplies separate Radon-representation and cutoff arguments before applying BV coarea/Sobolev, and retains Countable Choice. Neumann Poincaré uses connectedness, L1 compactness, zero-gradient constancy, bounded zero extension, and the two-dimensional full-space Sobolev inequality with their stated hypotheses. Relative and zero-extension perimeter conventions remain distinct.

The conductivity class uses the defined interior BV variation. The disk-inclusion calculation uses the graph flux identity with the correct outward-normal and distributional signs. The translation-modulus lemma assumes Countable Choice and applies bounded zero extension and translation to γ−1, rather than treating the nonintegrable background extension γ_e as a full-space BV function. Its Lp estimate follows from bounded differences and the L1 translation bound.
